title: Give static narration retakes new immutable audio URLs
acceptance: A changed encoded recitation take has a new content-addressed URL; previously published audio bytes remain at their old paths.
Both static recitation authoring commands publish the returned audio path, keep phrase lookup keys and timing metadata, and retain already generated files without unnecessary synthesis.

No production audio regeneration, voice/provider switch, account/session/entitlement change, paid call or deployment occurs in this source candidate. Listening quality and a later audio release require separate evidence.

evidence.note: Public HEAD at 2026-10-27T00:22Z: 200 audio/ogg, Cache-Control public,max-age=31536000,immutable; release.txt cff309ee209d88c5d1684c9d46dc3730218eb0c7. This establishes cache policy, not a demonstrated stale browser cache.

Real ffmpeg with original synthetic PCM tones. The encoder test failed against the old encoder; changed takes now have different digest paths and leave prior files intact. The real WAV conversion command preserves timing metadata and publishes a path that exists. No model/API used.

activity.summary: Claimed on isolated codex/tts-quality-selection after the user requested a new voice-quality/performance track. Diagnosis found static --force retakes reuse text-only URLs despite the immutable cache policy. The dormant website Plus selector candidate was independently rejected because the current site no longer loads it.
